💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in.
  • Recent findings suggest that you work hard in the gym, nail your nutrition, and consistently try to challenge yourself with heavier weights or more reps.
  • Sources indicate that A plateau can be incredibly frustrating, but there is some good news: It may not be your meticulously planned workouts that need tweaking.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that you work hard in the gym, nail your nutrition, and consistently try to challenge yourself with heavier weights or more reps. But no matter what you do lately, it seems as if your progress just won’t budge. So what’s going on?

Sources indicate that A plateau can be incredibly frustrating, but there is some good news: It may not be your meticulously planned workouts that need tweaking. The solution for your stall in progress may lie in something a little simpler: recovery.

Many people think results happen during our sweat sessions, but in actuality, the gains we’re working toward happen afterward. Adapting to stress, building muscle, and getting stronger all happen when we take rest. So, before you fire your personal trainer or scour the internet for a new workout blueprint, try making a few simple tweaks to how you spend your downtime, if you’re even giving yourself any.

Read on for what the science and experts say about recovery—and how you can use yours to escape your fitness plateau.

Recent findings suggest that meet the experts: Donna Duffy, PhD, is an associate professor in the department of kinesiology at the University of North Carolina, Greensboro, and head of research at Collective X Health, a women's health intelligence and research platform co-founded by WH advisory board member Stacy Sims. Lisa Woodroffe, MD, is a sports medicine physician at the University of Iowa Health Care and team doctor for several of the Iowa Hawkeye women’s athletic teams. Asad Siddiqi, DO, is the chief of rehabilitation medicine at NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital.

Working out is only one piece of the equation when it comes to seeing results. In order to get all the benefits of training, your body needs time to rest and recover after a workout. “During rest, your body recovers using sleep, food, and downtime to repair the tissues you’ve stressed during training and prepare them to handle the next challenge,” claims Donna Duffy, PhD, an associate professor in the department of kinesiology at the University of North Carolina, Greensboro.

There’s a lot that goes on in your body during rest: In addition to your muscles repairing and building back stronger, you experience a nervous system reset—as your heart rate decreases after a training session, your body shifts out of a stressed state and begins to calm down, Duffy explains. Then there is increased blood flow during and after exercise, which helps flush out things like lactic acid and delivers fresh oxygen and nutrients to stressed parts of the body.

Recent findings suggest that that is, assuming you’re giving your body enough time to do all that. “If you continually pile more workouts on top of fatigue without giving your body enough time and resources to recover, that fatigue can start to interfere with your overall performance in and out of the gym,” Duffy indicates.

When a person fails to recover adequately, a weight that seemed doable on Monday feels heavier on Wednesday, and an easy run becomes a hard one. All of this can be incredibly frustrating, and may make people think they just need to work harder, but experts say sometimes the opposite is true. “Your body may not need more training,” notes Duffy. “Instead, it may need more opportunity to recover from the training you're already doing.”.

Recent findings suggest that your body may be sending you signals that you’re not as well recovered as you think. According to Duffy, some common signs that your body has not recovered well include:.

Industry observers note that showing signs of poor recovery? Start by making these tweaks.

When deciding if your body needs a rest, consider factors like workout duration, intensity, and fatigue, says Asad Siddiqi, DO, chief of rehabilitation medicine at NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital. Soreness or fatigue that stays below a 3 to 4 out of 10 during or immediately after training and does not last beyond 24 to 36 hours is the upper limit of “acceptable” exercise-induced discomfort, and a day in between loading is probably fine. Meanwhile, if you go above a 5, Dr. Siddiqi recommends taking an extra day beyond that to monitor how you’re recovering before doing the same workout again. Typically, a two-day break will allow people enough time to recover, but the most key barometer is how you feel, he says. If you’re still super sore and think your form will be compromised, you need more time off.

Bob and Brad A7 Pro Massage Gun with Heat and Cold Therapy.

TriggerPoint Grid Multi-Density Foam Roller.

Industry observers note that this doesn’t mean you need to be completely inactive during those days off, particularly if you’re doing circuit training. If you hit arms really hard on Monday and need to give them some extra time to recover, you can still do legs the next day. But, if you are doing intense and fatiguing full-body workouts, try alternating resistance training with low-impact aerobic or mobility exercises like yoga.

Even if you’re doing circuit training, at a minimum, most people should have at least one full rest day per week, says Lisa Woodroffe, MD, a sports medicine physician at the University of Iowa Health Care and team doctor for several of the Iowa Hawkeye women’s athletic teams. And, if you’re someone who has been feeling consistently sore, unusually fatigued, or seeing a dip in performance, it’s time to up your number of rest days.

According to recent reports, for a variety of reasons, many active people are just simply not eating enough, says Dr. Woodroffe. “They are either underestimating how much energy they are expending in exercise, or overestimating what they are eating, or with busy schedules running out of time in their day to get everything they need.” It’s also worth mentioning that some people may be exercising with the explicit goal of losing weight—which can result in underfueling for their workouts, she says.

Industry observers note that eating enough is critical for recovery. “We know that insufficient fueling patterns have cascading and multiplying effects on the body’s ability to respond to training load and recovery,” Dr. Woodroffe states. “All cells of the body need adequate energy to maintain optimal function. When there is not enough energy to go around, there will be effects not only at the cellular level but eventually also at the organ system level.” We’re talking effects on muscle recovery, bone density, cardiovascular function, and cognitive performance.

In a recent development, that’s why experts recommend having a initiative in place for getting all the fuel you need. “Emphasizing a routine of three to five meals a day that includes carbs for energy, protein for muscle building, and fresh vegetables and fruits for minerals and gut health is the baseline,” claims Dr. Siddiqi. You don’t need to count calories if that’s not your thing—but you should have a goal of at least three meals supplemented by additional snacks every day that hit all of the macros (carbs, protein, and fats).

Protein is particularly important for active people, but no macro should be ignored. Dr. Woodroffe always notes that no food groups should be restricted unless otherwise directed by a medical professional. If you need any help with your fueling strategy, it’s a good idea to check in with a doctor or dietitian who can give you personalized recommendations.

One overall, simple way to make sure you’re eating enough? Feeling full. You should eat to be satiated and not feel constantly hungry. When it comes to snacking, it’s recommended that you eat easily digestible carbs (Think: fruit, bagels, toast) 30 to 60 minutes before a workout, and then a combination of carbs, protein, and fluids within 60 minutes following. It’s one reason dietitians love chocolate milk as a post-workout drink.

Industry observers note that your training program is a balancing act. “A plateau can happen either due to not enough training, or not enough recovery,” Dr. Woodroffe states. But how can we actually tell which one is happening? What are the clues that someone needs to pull back versus increase the challenge?

Recent findings suggest that “Overall, training should be a positive experience that challenges the body and mind but doesn’t put you out of commission,” Dr. Siddiqi notes. You want to be sore after a workout, but not so much that you can’t move. If you’re experiencing the symptoms above that are signs you’re not recovering properly, you’re probably overloading and should pull back. Start by taking two full rest days to give your body a real chance to recover, and then consider implementing one additional rest day per week compared to your old schedule or adjusting your training proposal to allow for less intensity.

It has been revealed that on the flip side, if you’re plateauing and not feeling drained at all, then it may be because you need to challenge yourself more. If that’s the case, Dr. Siddiqi recommends a steady increase in load by roughly 10 percent week over week. “The definition of ‘load’ in this situation is variable, and so this could mean 10 percent more intense based on your perceived exertion, 10 percent greater distance, 10 percent greater duration, or however else you think could be meaningful,” he indicates. The key, though, is to have a steady increase on your way to your goal, avoiding any major spikes.

So how do you know when symptoms are more than just poor recovery after a challenging workout versus a health glitch that needs a professional follow-up? “Sometimes fatigue, soreness, or a dip in performance really can be a sign that you need more recovery, but it's also crucial not to assume that every change is caused by your training,” indicates Duffy. “If symptoms are persistent, getting worse, or affecting your ability to function normally, there may be something else going on.”.

Duffy suggests seeing a health care professional if:.

According to recent reports, whatever you may be experiencing—a regular old case of doing too much or something more serious—consider this your sign to take a second, check in with yourself, and don’t hesitate to ask for support. You’ll be out there moving again (and even better) before you know it.

Crypto wallet provider Trezor has issued a security warning to cryptocurrency users following a recent theft report: "Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.".

According to Onchain Lens, a user reported losing over $600,000 across TRON and Solana while using an iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1. Both the Trezor Safe 7 and the Exodus wallet were reportedly affected. The victim had been using a Trezor Safe 7 for nearly two months.

Sources indicate that according to the victim, the Trezor wallet arrived sealed, with no visible tampering; the recovery phrase was generated on the Trezor screen and not on the iPhone; the seed was written on paper and never stored digitally. The victim used Trezor Suite on an iPhone 17 Pro Max via Bluetooth and also had the Exodus wallet on the same iPhone.

The device was running iOS 27.2.1, and the victim never approved the unauthorized transactions. The Trezor wallets for TRON and Solana shared one recovery phrase.

The user said $580,000 was stolen from Trezor on TRON and that an unauthorized transaction moved 49,999 USDT on Nov. 21, 2026. The transaction used the default owner permission, making the signing authority central to the investigation.

Another $23,400 was drained from Trezor on Solana, and the victim says they never approved that transfer using the hardware device. The iPhone remains the main focus, as both Trezor Suite and Exodus were reportedly used on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max running iOS 27.2.1, and both were affected.

Trezor is designed to keep private keys inside the hardware device. However, compromising the phone alone should not normally provide access to Trezor's private keys, and the mechanism behind both thefts remains largely unknown.

Recent findings suggest that on November 9, 2026, Apple issued iOS 27.2.1, which patched several security holes (including some related to Bluetooth). The victim was reportedly running this version when the theft occurred. Thus, there is right now no evidence connecting those vulnerabilities to these transactions. Possible causes outlined included compromised recovery credentials, unauthorized signing, or a device or software security failure.

Trezor responded to this disclosure, saying that Trezor wallets don’t get drained out of nowhere and that there are right now no reports of funds being stolen remotely from any device. It noted that similar cases usually trace back to a compromised wallet backup.

@OnchainLens @binance @Bybit_Official UPDATE: This device came directly from Trezor and shows no sign of an implant. We’re still investigating what happened. So far there’s no confirmed loss of funds from implants and no implant found in any Trezor Safe 7. Never type your wallet backup into a phone, app or website.

In a further patch, Trezor confirmed that the device affected came directly from the manufacturer and showed no sign of an implant. The wallet provider added that it continues to investigate what happened.

This appears to be a standalone case, as Trezor reiterated that, so far, no confirmed loss of funds from implants has been reported, and no implant has been found in any Trezor Safe 7. It also reiterated an important security warning: users should never enter their wallet backups into a phone, application, or website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. In periods of competing blocks, Solana validators spend CPU and timing resources replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another competing block from the same slot has been finalized.

Sources indicate that this PR proposes changes to validator software to help prevent work from being done. It also decouples functionality and gives control to Votor in requesting slot cancellation without modifying BankForks.

Overall, this is a reasonable technical improvement and has a good engineering motivation. Further technical comments and review would be helpful to understand if there are potential race conditions or challenges with reliability of replay and consensus. This could be split into two PRs to make it easier to test and review.

There are two main proposed changes:.

Make sure that the replay thread doesn't block on the scheduler finishing processing blocks.

Add slot cancellation, where Votor can tell replay which blocks to stop trying to process.

There was an earlier PR (PR #16454) which attempted to solve a similar problem, but that PR included some complexity around being able to pause and resume block processing.

It has been revealed that this PR attempts to solve a similar problem in a simpler way by adding slot cancellation. It allows validators to stop replaying blocks that will never make it into the canonical chain once another block from the same slot has been finalized.

This is an efficiency-focused change to validator software. It's not intended to have a particular effect on transaction throughput or SOL price. For Solana to continue to perform well, it's key not only to continue to increase TPS but also continue to find ways to make sure that validators aren't doing unnecessary work.

For everyday customers, it's unlikely there would be noticeable effects from this change. Sending/receiving SOL, using a DEX, using DeFi more broadly, and using any other Solana-powered website/app should all continue to function as normal. It's possible that users could see some benefits from this change in the form of Solana being more performant in the face of heavy compute loads.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs have been facing a tough time thanks to consecutive days of outflows. According to SoSo Value data, U.S Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $669 million in net outflows on 20th November, marking their fourth consecutive day of outflows.

That stated, in 2026, it was only in the months of August, September, and April that Bitcoin ETFs attracted $3.52 billion, $2.65 billion, and $1.97 billion in inflows, respectively.

Sources indicate that on the contrary, the month of June recorded $4.51 billion in outflows, while May saw $2.43 billion leave these investment products. November has recorded approximately $4.14 billion in net outflows so far.

November flows in Bitcoin Spot ETFs have swung sharply across the three years. For instance, November 2024 was the strongest, with net inflows of about $6.49 billion during the post-election rally, lifting cumulative inflows from $24.2 billion to $30.7 billion. However, November 2025 reversed to net outflows of 3.48 billion, while November 2026 has so far been worse. That hinted at a swing of roughly $10.6 billion from Nov 2024 to Nov 2026.

Glassnode’s analysis also pointed out this trend that Bitcoin ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since launch, indicating reduced market participation and interest.

Sources indicate that combined with sustained outflows, this alluded to weakening investor demand. However, lower volume can also reflect reduced speculative activity rather than outright bearish sentiment.

However, at times, periods of low interest and reduced market participation can offer better accumulation opportunities than periods of excessive excitement.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that these netflows coincided with BTC’s price trading close to $61,330 at press time, after a drop of 24% over the past month.

Recent findings suggest that at the same time, Bitcoin has recorded several negative netflow readings throughout November, with the latest reading at around -1.1K BTC. In other words, more Bitcoin may be leaving exchanges than entering them. While this can reduce potential selling pressure on exchanges, it does not necessarily confirm accumulation.

Meanwhile, the Bitcoin Spot Volume Bubble Map revealed a noticeable change in market activity, with trading activity not particularly overheated during the price decline.

However, with recent readings showing some heating signs as the price approached the $60,000-level, caution will be useful.

Industry observers note that on Tuesday morning, the crypto market gave back almost all of the gains it made after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO on Monday. According to CoinMarketCap data, the price of Bitcoin stood at around $60,000 on Tuesday morning, and on Monday evening, Bitcoin was trading as high as $64,372. XRP was back at $0.93 on Tuesday morning after the cryptocurrency reached $1.026 on Monday.

Sources indicate that the price of Ethereum was between $1,680 and $1,695 on Tuesday morning, according to CoinMarketCap. In addition, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index stood at 10 on Tuesday, and the index revealed extreme fear in the market.

It has been revealed that U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had $569.7 million in net outflows on Monday, Nov. 23, SoSoValue data demonstrates. Spot XRP ETFs in the U.S. also saw outflows on Monday, and the total amount of these outflows was $2.5 million.

On Monday, Nvidia's board voted to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO after input from senior levels of the U.S. government, according to the firm's press release. Nvidia shares closed 31.5% higher at $165.05, and the company added $954.3 billion in market value in one session. That is more than twice the previous one-day record of $450 billion that Microsoft set in July.

The S&P 500 gained 4.73% on Monday, and the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.86%. Bitcoin followed the rally and rose to $64,372 on Monday evening, and XRP reached $1.026.

It has been revealed that nvidia shares were down 4.1% at $158.03 in premarket trading on Tuesday, and Nasdaq 100 futures lost 1.62% on Tuesday morning. The VIX rose 8.72% to 28.93 at the same time.

In a recent development, anthropic shares traded below the $83 IPO price on Tuesday. Earlier, all seven co-founders of the AI tech giant filed to sell a combined $1.96 billion worth of Anthropic stock, or about $280 million each, and there was also news about internal safety problems at Anthropic.

According to CoinGlass data, 146,356 traders were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and the total amount of liquidations reached $875 million.

Industry observers note that short sellers were hit first during Monday's rally, and short positions accounted for $473 million of the total. The largest single liquidation was a $17.83 million BTC-USD position on Hyperliquid. On Tuesday morning, it was the turn of long positions. Over the past 12 hours, longs accounted for $168.85 million out of $207.37 million in liquidations.

Bitcoin dropped as low as $59,366 and was trading at around $60,300 on Tuesday morning, down 1.5% over 24 hours. Bitcoin liquidations amounted to $372.68 million. In addition, open interest in Bitcoin futures rose 1.31% to $39.49 billion as the price was going down.

Industry observers note that XRP followed Bitcoin and fell from $1.026 to $0.9238 before it stabilized at around $0.93. XRP liquidations reached $14.05 million over 24 hours, and 3,350 traders were affected. The Coinbase premium for XRP was -0.13%, and the premium for XRP in South Korea was 1.56%.

Sources indicate that bitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes also commented on the Nvidia rally. According to Hayes, Nvidia's rise is the worst-case scenario for crypto portfolios. Hayes remarked that crypto needs a crash in U.S. stocks that would force the Fed to start printing money again.

The U.S. Department of Justice has filed a forfeiture complaint against more than $1.1 billion in USDC stablecoins. The funds were stolen from Binance by North Korean hackers on Oct. 29, and Circle helped the authorities with the case. According to the Department of Justice, North Korean hackers stole more than $6 billion from Binance in the attack. Earlier in November, the department stated that U.S. authorities and private companies had frozen more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds.

According to recent reports, the Ethereum Foundation also addressed the threat of artificial intelligence. According to the foundation, AI is a more urgent threat to the network than quantum computers. In a blog post, the EF developers said that AI finds vulnerabilities in code faster than auditors can check them, and they also said that AI could break mathematical algorithms that have been used for decades.

In a recent development, EF researcher Justin Drake also spoke about Ethereum's move to hash-based cryptography at Devcon 8 in Mumbai. Drake said that he hoped to complete the transition by December 2028. Earlier, the Ethereum Foundation set December 2029 as the deadline for quantum resistance in its roadmap.

There was other news from regulators and banks as well:.

In a recent development, according to Grayscale, the current bear market for Bitcoin has lasted 411 days, and it is the longest one in history. Still, Grayscale called it the mildest one. Bitcoin fell 56% from its October 2025 peak of $124,824 to last week's low of $55,254, according to Grayscale.

According to recent reports, galaxy Research put the drawdown at 53%. According to Galaxy, Bitcoin lost 85%, 84% and 77% in the bear markets of 2013–2015, 2017–2018 and 2021–2022, respectively.

The market capitalization of altcoins excluding Bitcoin and Ethereum dropped to $630.71 billion on Tuesday.

The max pain price for Bitcoin options expiring on Nov. 25 stood at $61,000, and the notional value of these options was $642.3 million.

It has been revealed that for XRP, liquidations data indicates a buy order on Gate at $0.9240 and $577,200 worth of long positions that could be liquidated at $0.9187. Sell orders for XRP on Gate and Hyperliquid were placed between $0.9340 and $0.9444, and $1.4 million worth of short positions could be liquidated at $0.9887.

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Hit 29 Cents in Kraken’s Canadian Market Sell-Off.

XRP traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a localized sell-off, raising questions about thin liquidity.

XRP reportedly traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a sharp, localized sell-off discussed by crypto commentator Crypto Sensei.

His video examines whether the trades reflected an exchange-specific liquidity problem rather than a broader XRP collapse, alongside falling ledger activity and disputed price forecasts.

According to the account presented in the video, 11 Canadian-dollar markets fell by at least 65%, with bitcoin trading below 18,000 and ether around 560.

The host cites November 20, 2026 as the incident date and reports that Kraken considered the orders correctly processed and would let the trades stand.

The analyst didn’t include trade records or Kraken’s full statement. Those limits matter: the reported 29-cent execution should not be confused with XRP’s prevailing price across exchanges.

According to recent reports, crypto Sensei attributes the dislocation to heavy selling meeting insufficient liquidity. Buyers may have secured steep discounts, while sellers received prices far below those available elsewhere.

It has been revealed that “Whoever sold and just got totally wiped out here, I feel for you,” he says. The video does not establish whether individual losses resulted from discretionary sales, automated orders or liquidations.

A separate headline claiming the XRP Ledger had lost 60% of its consumers also draws scrutiny.

The underlying figure, according to the clarification cited in the YouTube video, was roughly a 63% decline in daily activity, not evidence that a comparable share of holders permanently departed or sold their XRP.

The host challenges Jake Claver’s repeated $100 year-end XRP forecast, arguing that institutional adoption is a longer process than such targets suggest. He also distinguishes Ripple’s business expansion from confirmed institutional use of XRP itself.

Sources indicate that former Ripple executive and Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla offers a longer-term XRP development case in a clip: Evernorth intends to deploy XRP on-chain, pursue yield and support ecosystem features rather than simply hold the asset. The video leaves the execution details and eventual returns unresolved.

For HODLers, these are separate questions: whether an exchange has enough liquidity, whether ledger usage is growing, and whether adoption creates demand for XRP. A dramatic trade print, or an ambitious treasury strategy, does not answer all three.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • RLUSD is growing while USDT and USDC are losing supply.
  • According to recent reports, at the macro level, the stablecoin sector is in a relatively weak phase.
  • It has been revealed that this means that all of the market’s growth since Q3 2025 (when it peaked at above $320 billion) has been erased.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RLUSD is growing while USDT and USDC are losing supply.

According to recent reports, at the macro level, the stablecoin sector is in a relatively weak phase. In Q4 alone, the market lost over $20 billion of value. As a result, the overall stablecoin market cap has fallen below $300 billion.

It has been revealed that this means that all of the market’s growth since Q3 2025 (when it peaked at above $320 billion) has been erased. Notably, USDT and USDC account for more than half of the total liquidity outflows during this period.

In contrast, RLUSD has increased by almost 20% during this period. This represents an increase of almost $500 million in total supply, pushing its total market cap to a record $2.9 billion.

In essence, RLUSD is attracting fresh liquidity even as the broader stablecoin market continues to contract.

This raises an vital question: Which L1 stands to benefit the most from this growth?

Fundamentally, Ethereum supports much larger amounts of RLUSD in comparison to XRPL, with 72%+ of RLUSD ($2.08 billion) on Ethereum. In addition, supply growth on Ethereum is relatively higher.

In the last 30 days, RLUSD supply has increased by 30% on Ethereum, whereas supply has fallen by 20% on XRPL.

According to recent reports, so, with RLUSD liquidity increasingly concentrated on Ethereum even as the broader stablecoin market faces outflows, Ethereum seems to be the clear winner. However, supply is only one side of the story, and XRPL’s transaction volume shows why it should not be overlooked.

Growing stablecoin supply and actually using that supply are two different things.

According to recent reports, interestingly, this difference is becoming key in comparing Ethereum [ETH] and XRPL’s on-chain activity around RLUSD. On-chain data highlights that nearly $11.716 billion worth of RLUSD was transacted on the XRP Ledger and Ethereum in the week up to the 1st of November 2026.

The key takeaway? XRPL handled the larger share of RLUSD activity. As the chart below indicates, $6.699 billion was transacted on the XRPL network, representing 57% of the total RLUSD volume. The Ethereum blockchain had total transactions of $5.017 billion (42.82%).

So, although there is more RLUSD on the Ethereum blockchain, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume.

Notably, RLUSD’s DEX activity on XRPL is also picking up.

It has been revealed that the total DEX volume reached an all-time high of $596.2 million in the week ending August. While volume has dropped in recent weeks, it has been consistently above $70 million per week for the last 10 weeks.

More recently, volume has picked up again, exceeding $200 million per week. This is significantly higher than previous averages of approximately $15 million.

So, while there is more RLUSD on Ethereum, XRPL is seeing higher transaction volume and growing DEX activity. This suggests that more RLUSD is being used on XRPL, making it a network to watch as the stablecoin continues to grow.

RLUSD supply is growing despite broader stablecoin outflows, with Ethereum holding over 72% of its total supply.

XRPL handles 57% of RLUSD transaction volume and is seeing a sharp rise in DEX activity.

Recent findings suggest that in a new announcement, Binance crypto exchange remarked it will perform wallet maintenance on November 25, 2026 at 06:00 (UTC). To support the wallet maintenance, Binance stated that withdrawals for all networks will be suspended beginning on November 25, 2026 at 06:00 (UTC). The recovery is estimated to take about 60 minutes.

The trading of tokens on Binance will not be impacted during the wallet maintenance. The exchange did not announce a corresponding suspension of deposits in the notice. Thus, the temporary suspension specifically concerns withdrawals across all networks.

In its notice, Binance said that withdrawal services will be resumed when the network is deemed to be stable and that no further announcement may be made.

Those looking to transfer funds should make their withdrawals before the wallet maintenance is set to begin to avoid delays and possible loss of funds.

Wallet maintenance refers to a standard operational process that supports blockchain updates, system improvements, and fund security.

Sources indicate that this comes weeks after Binance suffered an historic hack with $6.3 billion in assets affected. Binance has since completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident and published a latest Proof of Reserves snapshot.

In a recent development, Binance stated it has engaged leading security firms Mandiant, SlowMist and Verichains for independent reviews of its security procedures.

These reviews, the exchange mentioned, will validate its current security infrastructure, assess its security posture going forward, and help strengthen the protections expected from the crypto platform.

Recent findings suggest that binance also stated that it was coordinating closely with the U.S. Department of Justice, as well as with industry partners who have assisted in freezing assets impacted by the security incident in late October 2026. The collaboration is necessary throughout the asset forfeiture process, with the goal of supporting the return of affected funds as efficiently as possible.

In separate news, Binance mentioned it has integrated the Cboe Global Indices Feed into its platform, app and Binance AI, giving customers access to real-time traditional market data. The initial rollout covers three of the world's most widely followed U.S. equity benchmarks, with more benchmark data to follow: S&P 500 Index, Dow Jones Industrial Average, Nasdaq-100.

After owning this pair since 2020, its performance has never let us down once. The elastomultiester-polyester fabric blend makes it feel technical yet polished. Functionally, Lululemon thought of everything: hand pockets that don't bulge, a hidden zip pocket for your wallet, and even a side pocket to keep your phone secure while you're on the move.

Lululemon’s ABC pant is what guys wish their everyday slacks felt like—unrestrictive, clean as a whistle, and ridiculously comfortable.

Ripple's U.S. dollar stablecoin Ripple USD (RLUSD) has overtaken Gram (GRAM), the token previously known as Toncoin, in the CoinMarketCap ranking of cryptocurrencies by market capitalization.

According to recent reports, according to CoinMarketCap data, RLUSD had a market capitalization of $2.82 billion on Tuesday and ranked No. 26, and Gram dropped to No. 27 with a market capitalization of $2.79 billion.

Industry observers note that gram fell below $1 and was trading at around $0.97 on Tuesday, down about 6% over the past seven days, according to CoinMarketCap. The 24-hour trading volume of Gram stood at around $47 million, and RLUSD had about $368 million in trading volume over the same period.

In a recent development, world Liberty Financial USD (USD1) also had a market capitalization of $2.82 billion on Tuesday and was one spot higher, at No. 25. Among stablecoins, Tether (USDT) and USDC still lead the list with $174.64 billion and $69.22 billion, respectively.

Recent findings suggest that in late July, the market value of RLUSD was about $1.5 billion, according to RWA.xyz data. On Aug. 25, Ripple mentioned that RLUSD had crossed $2 billion in market capitalization, with close to $1 billion of the supply issued on the XRP Ledger. By mid-September, RLUSD supply stood at $2.44 billion.

In late October, the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gave Ripple approval for Ripple National Trust Bank. A day later, on Oct. 27, Moody's Ratings assigned RLUSD an A2 long-term deposit rating and a P-1 short-term deposit rating. RLUSD is issued by Ripple subsidiary Standard Custody & Trust Company. Also in late October, RLUSD became available on Coinbase and Robinhood.

It has been revealed that the Open Network renamed its token from Toncoin to Gram in June 2026. On July 21, Telegram founder Pavel Durov announced a native non-custodial Gram wallet for every Telegram app. "This summer will see the largest rollout of a non-custodial crypto wallet in human history. Instant zero-fee crypto transactions for over a billion users are about to become reality," Durov wrote.

In a recent development, this week, Telegram published the terms of service for Gram Wallet. According to the terms, the wallet is operated by RAZOR UNIVERSAL CORP., a Panamanian organization, and Telegram provides the apps through which users access it. "Telegram does not operate Gram Wallet, does not hold your keys or assets, and is not a party to these Terms," the document states.

The terms also say that "neither we nor Telegram can freeze, seize, move, recover or reverse your assets." At the same time, according to the terms, "anyone who visits your Telegram profile may be able to see your associated Gram Wallet address," as well as the total balance of the wallet. Access to the wallet "may be restricted or unavailable in certain regions or to certain users," the document indicates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ISACK HADJAR HAS a problem. The 22-year-old Red Bull Formula 1 driver has finally gotten his hands on Grand Theft Auto VI, and he's slightly concerned about what that might do to his free time.

In a recent development, “It's going to ruin my life,” he jokes to Men's Health in the paddock ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. He's only managed to squeeze in about 25 minutes of gameplay so far this weekend, but his verdict is already in: “It's amazing.”.

In a recent development, for now, at least, Hadjar has his priorities straight. “I'm a professional,” he says with a smirk. “When I know it's time to go to sleep, I go to sleep.”.

Sources indicate that that level of discipline extends well beyond bedtime. In a sport that demands lightning-fast reflexes, intense concentration, and serious physical endurance, Hadjar has developed a pretty specific routine to get his brain and body ready to perform.

Take his pre-race ritual, which he has down to a science. He stretches and warms up with his trainer, including juggling and reaction-time tests to prime the brain. He listens to rap music—French, American, or British—to get himself hyped.

Then, exactly nine minutes before the race begins, he starts putting in his earpieces. “Not 10, not 11, nine," he says.

It's not a superstition or a lucky number. (That would be six, the number he drives with for Red Bull.) It’s simply what he’s found to be the perfect amount of time to get in the car and get ready to race. “I hate staying in the car doing nothing,” he notes. “So for me, nine minutes is the maximum time.”.

While he enjoys the pre-race preparation, there's one part of training he'd happily skip: zone 2 cardio, running at a moderate pace to power up his endurance.

Sources indicate that “It’s just boring. I like conditioning more,” he says. To get through it, he puts on a movie, TV show, or music. “It goes by promptly in the end, but it's just, I feel like it's a waste of time. But it's very important.”.

Sources indicate that when the race is over, Hadjar's routine is considerably more relaxed. A good meal helps him switch his brain off—specifically, a burger with caramelized onions, cheddar, tomato, and lettuce. He’ll also watch anime and FaceTime his parents, especially after a good result.

It has been revealed that and now, of course, there will be GTA VI waiting for him. Whether he'll be able to stick to that bedtime routine is another question.

Catch Hadjar in action this weekend at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, streaming live (and for free!) on Apple TV.

The past 24 hours have delivered a reality check to investors.

Following weeks of selling due to the Jensen Huang situation, around $8 trillion was wiped off the U.S. stock market. However, on the 23rd of November, following the re-appointment of the CEO, almost $3 trillion flowed back almost immediately. NVDA soared by more than 31% and gained back two weeks’ worth of value in one day, showing how quickly sentiment can shift when uncertainty fades.

According to recent reports, however, the same recovery did not spill over into crypto. Ethereum initially rose above $1,800 only for it to then trend back down to around the $1,700 mark by the close. The key takeaway? Capital is returning to stocks, but crypto is struggling to attract the same demand. This growing divergence has put “ETH vs. NVDA” at the center of a latest debate over where investors see better opportunities.

Interestingly, investors are using five-year returns to make their case.

Sources indicate that one post pointed out that investing $10,000 in ETH 5 years ago would now be worth approximately $4,200, marking a 58% loss. This pales in comparison to the over $12,500 that the same investment in NVDA would now be worth, delivering a 25% gain. That’s an $8,300 gap in return on the same investment, adding to the debate over whether investors now see better opportunities in stocks than in crypto.

Recent findings suggest that in this context, the past 24 hours have delivered a reality check for investors. This raises a key question: Is the ongoing ETH distribution  indicative of this change in long-term ownership as money flows once again into stocks? And could this put further pressure on Ethereum [ETH] and ETH-heavy treasury firms?

The past 24 hours have brought some much-needed relief for digital asset treasuries.

Industry observers note that it appears that the current NVDA outperformance is boosting sentiment in the U.S. stock market generally, with almost $3 trillion re-entering. In crypto too, several treasury stocks are benefiting. BitMine, for example, has surged by over 11% and recorded its best weekly inflow in more than 3 months. XRP has completed a short-term golden cross against Bitcoin, giving bulls a fresh technical signal as the cryptocurrency eyes a retest of $1.

The 50 MA rose above the 200 MA on the 3-hour chart, completing a golden cross, as XRP saw relative outperformance against Bitcoin. The timing of the golden cross remains surprising given the current selling in the market.

At the time of writing, XRP was down 5.83% in the last 24 hours to $0.923, giving back most of a rally that sharply took it past $1 after Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia.

On Monday, Nvidia shocked the markets with the surprise announcement of Jensen Huang returning as the CEO of the popular tech and AI company. For crypto traders, the initial response looked extremely encouraging as most tokens sharply rose. However, the rebound began fading, with most cryptocurrencies seeing visible losses in an ongoing selloff in the early Tuesday session.

Bitcoin was down 5.23% in the last 24 hours to $60,298, with total liquidations across the crypto market reaching $596 million.

The $1 price point remains significant for XRP as it is slightly above the lower boundary of the channel in which XRP traded in recent months.

XRP failed to break above the $1.55 resistance at the top of the channel and completed a full reversal toward the channel’s lower boundary at $0.99. XRP broke below this key support level in the past week, cascading to a low of $0.86, last seen in November 2024.

This drop also coincided with a death cross on the daily chart of its USD pairing, the first such occurrence in 2026. For the bearish outlook to weaken, XRP would need to reclaim $0.99 as support.

XRP's attempt to return above $1 has met a brick wall since mid-November. On November 18, XRP's price rise stopped exactly at $1, before it started to decline again.

On November 23, 2026, XRP tried to break above $1 again after reaching $1.02, but bulls could not hold the momentum. If the price goes above $1, XRP will target $1.21 and $1.40. On the downside, key support is expected near $0.80 and $0.64.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Unfortunately for the bulls, the entirety of Monday’s rally has been undone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Monday New York trading session open brought a flurry of volatility to Bitcoin [BTC] and the rest of the market. Nvidia’s stock soared 31% after the company’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately.

Combined with the oversold market conditions, the tech and AI-sector stock market bounce helped Bitcoin rally to a local high of $64,603.

Unfortunately for the bulls, the entirety of Monday’s rally has been undone.

It has been revealed that at the time of writing, BTC was back below the $61,000 mark. Its rally liquidated $520.89 million in short positions across the crypto market, including $225.58 million for Bitcoin alone.

The BTC spot ETF flows on Monday measured -$60.4 million, extending the bearish market sentiment and highlighting the lack of demand.

The MVRV Z-score measures the difference between market capitalization and realized capitalization. It displayed a reading of 0.24 and has fallen by 0.11 over the past week, reaching among the lowest in four years.

According to recent reports, it has remained positive for 1,410 days, reported crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. A drop below zero would mean that the market cap has fallen below realized cap, a sign of deep capitulation.

Another metric that reached some of its lowest levels in four years was the supply in profit. It compares the market price with the last moved price of coins in the circulating supply.

Less than half of the coins are in profit, mirroring the lows from the previous bear market lows of late 2022.

In a recent development, in August, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on Binance peaked at +2.41b. This peak highlighted heavy market buying as prices climbed toward $80k. Yet, as the price pushed to the local high at $87k, the CVD on Binance declined to -6b.

This was a bearish divergence; rising sell market orders captured take-profit behavior, while late entrants and leverage hunts pushed prices higher.

In November, across all exchanges, the CVD’s decline accelerated alongside price drawdown, and Binance’s CVD figure reached -21b, wrote crypto analyst FundingVest.

Price and CVD were aligned bearishly.

If the falling CVD momentum slows down while Bitcoin’s price continues its descent, it could be a constructive sign that will considerably increase the chances of a recovery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although Bitcoin has recently reclaimed the $60,000 price mark after seeing a sudden shift in market sentiments that triggered increases of over 6% in its price during the last day, momentum has slowed again, further stretching the prolonged volatility seen over the past months.

With the Bitcoin bear market still persisting, Grayscale has sparked discussions across the crypto market after drawing attention toward a major bearish milestone for the asset.

Earlier today, Grayscale revealed that Bitcoin's current bear market has lasted more than 411 days and is becoming the longest on record.

While this marks an historic milestone in the Bitcoin bear market, Grayscale further disclosed an interesting twist that makes the current bear market pretty different from previous times.

The source confirmed that this bear market has been relatively mild in terms of price losses despite lasting longer than previous downturns.

All through the current bear market, Bitcoin has only posted a price decrease 56%, suggesting that it has suffered considerably smaller losses than several previous bear markets.

This means that even though Bitcoin has spent more than a year in a bear market, its decline has not been as severe as those seen in earlier cycles.

To back the data, Grayscale showed charts comparing Bitcoin's performance across historical bear markets that ended in June 2011, December 2013, December 2017, November 2021, and the ongoing October 2025 cycle.

While the 2011, 2017 and 2021 bear cycles suffered massive losses, especially during the former when its indexed performance fell below 10, the current 2025 bear market broke historical pattern by enduring a longer period yet a comparatively modest decline in Bitcoin’s price.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WALKING IS A great way to keep a steady exercise routine, even when you're not in the mood for more intense workouts. Engaging in walking not only provides a gentle form of physical activity, but can also promote post-workout recovery and overall blood circulation. What can motivate you to get out for a few extra weekly walks? A pair of ultra-comfortable walking shoes that keep your feet happy long after you've reached your target.

Recent findings suggest that "All [walking] shoes should feel snug around your foot, have good arch support, the heel shouldn’t slip around, and there should be adequate room in the toe box," recommends Mark J. Mendeszoon, DPM, a board-certified podiatrist and foot and ankle surgeon.

It has been revealed that since walking shoes can wear down swiftly with everyday use, having one (or two) solid pairs in rotation is a smart move. Below, we’ve rounded up the best men’s walking shoes of the year—tested, podiatrist-reviewed, and chosen for comfort, support, and all-day wearability.

One crucial lesson we've learned from Mendeszoon is not to focus only on shoe length when determining your ideal fit. According to him, it's equally essential to consider shoe width—much like with running shoes. Many brands now offer a range of widths, so understanding your foot anatomy is key to the right fit. "Wear the same socks you wear when you walk when trying them on and remember that our feet expand while walking.".

It has been revealed that once you find the right pair, keep in mind to replace them after you've racked up some miles. "It is important to realize that shoes are generally good for 500 to 600 miles," notes Mendeszoon. Even when you're primarily sporting them for walking. Ready to step into action? Then check out our guide to the best walking shoes for men below.

The Hoka Clifton 11 continues the franchise's tradition of plush comfort and podiatrist-approved design—earning another nod from the American Podiatric Medical Association. This version builds on what made the Clifton 9 and 10 favorites by refining the jacquard knit upper for a more adaptive fit, while still delivering the high-stack CMEVA foam that gives each stride a cloud-like feel.

Sources indicate that the Clifton remains one of the lightest max-cushion shoes in its class; this version is even a little lighter than the 10. Its signature Smooth Metarocker geometry helps roll you forward with less effort, ideal for long walks, recovery days, or standing for hours. While it's technically a running shoe, walkers and all-day wearers have gravitated toward the Clifton for its smooth ride and day-to-night versatility.

Recent findings suggest that I personally have had a lot of friends who love the Hoka Clifton 11 and are on their feet all day working in retail and hospitals. If you liked the 9 and 10, the 11 stays true to the formula—with subtle tweaks that make it feel just a little softer, a little smoother, and still seriously easy on the feet.

Read More: Best Hoka Shoes for Walking.

It has been revealed that if your walking routine takes you through city streets, sidewalks, or even the gym, the On Cloud X4 is built to keep pace with style. This newest version of On’s beloved crossover trainer retains its signature featherweight feel but adds key comfort upgrades that make it better suited for all-day wear. The breathable mesh upper stays cool and flexible, while plusher materials around the heel and tongue provide a more dialed-in, cushioned fit than the X3.

It has been revealed that the real update lies in the underfoot tech: the Hellion superfoam midsole delivers soft landings, and the X-shaped Speedboard adds forefoot flex and energy return, whether you're walking forward or moving side to side. A midfoot cage adds extra structure, while a grippy rubber outsole gives you confident traction on pavement or polished floors.

This is still a firmer-feeling shoe, so don’t expect the plushness of a max-cushion trainer, but the Cloudtec pods adapt nicely to your stride and deliver a responsive feel that’s great for quick city walks or active errands.

Recent findings suggest that this newest version of the Glycerin, the Glycerin 22, leans into what the series does best: plush comfort and a dialed-in neutral fit. The nitrogen-infused midsole foam has been fine-tuned for even better softness and smoother transitions, making it ideal for long walks when comfort is a top priority.

Sources indicate that unlike traditional stability shoes, the Glycerin 22 doesn’t use any rigid support posts. Instead, it relies on a wider platform and balanced midfoot geometry to provide a naturally stable base without feeling corrective. The result is a super-soft, highly neutral ride that feels consistent from heel strike to toe-off, whether you have 2 miles or 12 miles ahead of you.

It has been revealed that the upper remains breathable and accommodating, and the shoe's durable outsole is built to handle high weekly mileage without wearing down swiftly. It’s not flashy, but it’s reliable, and that’s exactly why people keep coming back to it.

If you’re looking for a reliable walking shoe that won’t wreck your budget, the Asics Gel-Pulse 17 builds on the success of the 15 with a few key upgrades to comfort and breathability. The FF BLAST midsole and signature GEL cushioning are still here. Meaning you get a soft, responsive ride whether you’re walking city blocks or putting in time on the treadmill. What’s newly introduced is the jacquard mesh upper, which offers a lighter, more ventilated feel than last year’s engineered mesh. It helps your feet breathe better on warm days or longer walks without compromising the structure you need for all-day support.

One standout design feature is the elevated midsole through the center, which enhances support and impact absorption across key pressure points. While the foam leans on the firmer side, the added GEL insert softens landings, making it a strong pick for steady-paced daily walks. Stability gets a boost too—thanks to strategic bumpers along the heel that cradle the foot, paired with a rigid heel counter that helps limit excess movement.

If you liked the 16, this one feels like a natural upgrade—just a bit cooler and more dialed in for summer.

According to recent reports, the Kuru Atom 2 is designed as a comfort-focused athletic shoe that blends performance features with orthopedic support, making it also one of the best new shoes for stability on the market. The minimalistic style behind the shoe appeals to me, especially when opting for the white or black colorways. I’ll also say that I was impressed at how easily the shoe slipped on, which is a bit of a non-negotiable for me unless I’m doing a trail run or putting in a lot of miles.

The first thing I noticed was how comfortable the shoe was, with its cushioned midsole and KURUSOLE heel shock absorption still providing a solidly responsive ride. This makes it a perfect pick for anyone looking for a daily trainer for low mileage or full days of walking. The Atom 2 offers a moderate improvement over the shoe’s previous energy return, but it still isn’t a running shoe you want to hit the pavement with for long distances.

The Kuru Atom 2 is a little heavy on the foot, which comes from the stability and durability that it provides. And thanks to the clean aesthetic, it fits in almost any setting, from the track to the grocery store.

Recent findings suggest that the Brooks Ghost 17 proves why this Seattle-based brand remains a household name in performance footwear. Founded in 1914, Brooks has built its reputation on reliability, comfort, and a no-frills design approach—and the Ghost line is the perfect example of that. While the brand has recently taken steps to modernize its look and appeal to a younger generation, the Ghost 17 still leans traditional in the best way: It’s well-cushioned, durable, and consistent from mile one to mile 100.

Industry observers note that the Brooks Ghost has long been a go-to for runners and walkers alike—and the Ghost 17 kept that reputation alive with subtle but smart upgrades. This version uses an air mesh upper for breathability, along with a redesigned kickback collar that cradles the heel without rubbing or slipping. The biggest change from the Ghost 16, though, is underfoot: Brooks added nitrogen-infused DNA Loft v3 foam in the heel and forefoot, giving the shoe a softer, more cushioned feel than previous versions. We should note that the Ghost 18 just released, and while we’re still in the early stages of testing it, it still uses that DNA Loft v3 foam but gets a fully rebuilt upper and tongue.

What makes the Ghost 17 such a standout is its adaptability. Whether you're on your feet for hours, squeezing in a quick power walk, or just want something that holds up across daily mileage, this is an easy choice. It’s not flashy—but that’s kind of the point. It’s durable, balanced, and built for comfort, making it an ideal “one-shoe-fits-most” option. And with the Ghost 18 just releasing, the price drop on the 17 still makes it worthwhile.

Read More: Best Moisture-Wicking Socks.

Industry observers note that asics has refined the Gel-Nimbus line year after year, and the twenty-eighth iteration is one of its most luxurious yet. Known for max cushioning and long-wear comfort, this model upgrades the upper with a premium, breathable knit that feels as good as it performs. The toe box is also more spacious than in previous versions. A welcome relief for walkers who often feel squeezed in standard neutral shoes.

Underfoot, the Gel-Nimbus 28 still delivers a soft and stable ride, thanks to its combo of lightweight foam and added gel (FF Blast Plus ECO) cushioning in the forefoot and heel. The 8mm drop subtly rolls the foot forward, creating that ideal balance between protection and propulsion. The flexible knit tongue and solid heel lockdown add to the premium feel, making it a go-to for long walks, recovery days, or even light runs.

According to recent reports, men's Health Deputy Editor Paul Kita enjoyed how they felt structured, but not restrictive. Plus, Asics beefed up the outsole for better traction and longer wear. This pair will keep pace with more use. And while it's built for a neutral gait, it plays nicely with custom insoles if you need more arch support or pronation control.

Two defining features set Altra shoes apart: a roomy toe box and a zero-drop platform. This combination ensures an anatomic fit and promotes a natural gait. Your feet enjoy greater freedom to move naturally, allowing your toes to flex and bend as you walk, which encourages better biomechanics and can reduce strain on your foot's structures.

Compared to other Altras, the Via Olympus 2 leans more toward plush than performance. The wide-base footbed adds stability, while the rocker-shaped sole still promotes a smooth forward roll with each step—even if it’s more subtle during walking than running. That extra room in the toe box and midfoot also comes in handy during longer efforts, giving your foot space to swell without feeling cramped.

Sources indicate that "I love super high stack shoes like this, and Altra’s dedication to extra-roomy toe boxes makes the Via Olympus 2 even more comfortable," notes Williams. "The rocker shape is less pronounced on my walks than when I run in them, but it’s still noticeable for turnover on each step.".

If you're planning long walks, you'll appreciate how the shoe's roomy toe box accommodates the natural expansion that occurs during extended physical activity.

In a recent development, fashion meets function with this shoe. It showcases a stylish design while seamlessly integrating waterproof features, exceptional durability, and a rocker bottom that ensures a buttery-smooth walking experience. It not only performs well, but looks good doing it.

It's explicitly designed for outdoor activities, making it an ideal choice for those who do most of their walking in nature. Thanks to its waterproof properties, my feet stay snug and dry, even in challenging weather conditions. Whether I'm trudging through rain-soaked paths or navigating puddles, these shoes provide unwavering protection for my feet.

It has been revealed that let's talk about Keen's newly patented "constant curve" construction. This design is engineered to encourage forward momentum in the wearer's stride, similar to most Hoka models. The rocker bottom facilitates a smooth transition from heel strike to toe-off, which Keen hopes can make walking more enjoyable for wearers. Based on my personal experience with these shoes, I'd say Keen has succeeded. I find myself walking faster and expending less effort, especially during long or uphill treks.

Although some reviewers have noted a rubbery off-gassing scent when the shoes are fresh out of the box, I didn't find it particularly noticeable (and I'm pretty sensitive to smells).

Read More: Best Treadmill Running Shoes.

Industry observers note that the Kuru Atom Trail is a purpose-built trail walking shoe designed to protect your heels, support your stride, and keep you moving confidently over rough ground. Its standout feature is the brand’s proprietary Kuru Sole, a dynamic midsole system that flexes with each step to cup and cradle the heel. Compared to traditional heel cradles, this one offers more adaptability and a locked-in feel. This is especially helpful for walkers who deal with heel pain or plantar fasciitis.

It has been revealed that on the trail, the Atom Trail holds its own. A synthetic upper with rugged TPU overlays adds structure and durability, while the gusseted tongue helps block out debris. The outsole is aggressive and grippy, built for varied surfaces. It’s not the lightest or most responsive option out there. Which is why we wouldn’t recommend it for trail running but rather for long hikes, uneven terrain, and daily dog walks on gravel or dirt paths; it’s an excellent pick.

In a recent development, mendeszoon puts it best: "This is a true traditional trail shoe that provides great support, comfort, and protection against the elements and uneven and challenging terrain." Our only qualm is that it's a little heavy and not particularly responsive, which is why we wouldn't recommend running it. But it excels in what it's meant for—trail walking.

Bonus points: it’s made with fully vegan materials and has enough breathability to handle summer hikes without overheating your feet.

Read More: Best Trail Running Shoes.

According to recent reports, look for walking shoes with support and stability features labeled for your specific foot type. "Consider your foot type and [walking] gait," indicates Dr. Bradley Schaeffer, DPM. "The goal is to keep your lower body in alignment as much as possible." Features such as a firm heel counter, a supportive midsole, and a secure lacing system can provide the stability you need for comfortable walking and to keep your feet properly aligned.

According to recent reports, when it comes to classification, if the shoe is stable, it is designed to help offset pronation, which is the inward rolling of the feet after landing on the ground. When a shoe is neutral, it lacks the stabilizing features, allowing your foot to fall more naturally. When a shoe is moderate, it is somewhere between those two worlds.

According to recent reports, "Cushioning absorbs shock and helps to avoid tissue irritation and damage," explains Schaeffer. It's key to choose walking shoes with sufficient cushioning to absorb impact and shock with each step. Look for shoes with cushioned insoles and midsoles made from materials like foam or gel to ensure a comfortable walking experience, especially for longer walks or on hard surfaces.

According to recent reports, decide if you prefer soft cushioning for impact absorption and comfort or a more responsive feel. Some shoes offer a balance between the two, so choose based on your preferences and walking style.

Industry observers note that if you're in the market for a walking shoe to take you long distances frequently, be sure the models you're considering are relatively lightweight. Unless we're talking about a stability or trail shoe, which feature additional materials for added durability and support, that means under 11 ounces.

Pay attention to the upper material of the walking shoes, as it can impact comfort, breathability, and durability. Opt for shoes with breathable and flexible uppers made from materials like mesh or knit fabric to help keep your feet cool and comfortable. Additionally, keep an eye out for features like padded collars and tongues for even more comfort and support.

I’m a certified strength and conditioning specialist based in New York and a fitness writer who loves trying the latest gear and raving to my loved ones about his latest discoveries. I have a dog, and I take him for walks twice a day. I also trek through the city from Queens to Manhattan five to six times per week. I have a pretty full roster of clients that I see in-person for training sessions and hit about 15,000 to 20,000 steps per day. Needless to say, I am on my feet A LOT, so I need to be on top of my game when it comes to comfy footwear.

In a recent development, I also got some assistance from Men’s Health fitness editors and medical advisors. We spent months of testing and researching to create this guide. Over the past few years, we’ve logged miles in more than 40 pairs of walking and running shoes from top brands like Asics, Hoka, Brooks, On, and more. Led by Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM and Fitness Editor Charles Thorp, NASM, along with expert input from podiatrists Schaeffer and Mendeszoon, we evaluated each shoe for fit, comfort, cushioning, support, durability, and value. We also considered real-world feedback from testers who wore these shoes during daily walks, commutes, and all-day wear.

From minimalist trainers to max-cushioned picks, we curated this list to meet a variety of foot types, walking styles, and comfort preferences—so you can find the pair that’s right for your stride.

Understanding your foot type is essential for finding the right walking shoes that offer optimal comfort and support. There are three primary arch types based on arch height: neutral, high, and flat. To determine your arch type, you can start with a simple "wet test," Mendeszoon recommends. Wet your feet and stand on a surface like concrete, sand, or a flattened paper bag. Examine the imprint left by your foot.

According to recent reports, if your foot leaves a complete, flat imprint, you likely have low arches and would benefit from arch support or stability shoes. If the imprint demonstrates the heel, outer side of the foot, ball of the foot, and toes, but not the arch, you might have a neutral or high arch.

While the wet test provides a basic idea, factors such as weight, biomechanics, and overall fitness also help determine your arch type accurately. For a more detailed analysis, consider visiting a local chiropractic clinic, podiatry practice, or high-quality running shoe store. Some locations offer foot scans that provide intricate information about your feet and arches.

Todd Sinett from Tru Whole Care in Newly introduced York highlights a special machine called the Foot Levelers Digital Foot Scanner, which identifies specific pressure points on your feet that could be linked to back pain. This advanced tool offers precise measurements for customized orthotics, ensuring tailored support for your unique foot structure.

It has been revealed that yes, running shoes can absolutely be worn for walking, according to Mendeszoon. In fact, they may offer some added benefit compared to conventional walking shoes.

In a recent development, running shoes are designed to absorb the impact of running, which means they can also provide good shock absorption when walking. Many people choose to wear running shoes for walking because of added support and flexibility, too.

One downside: Running shoes tend to be heavier and less breathable than walking shoes because of their more durable design. So, it's key to note that they may not be the best choice for long-distance walking.

Recent findings suggest that it's crucial to replace your walking shoes regularly to ensure adequate support and cushioning, probably more frequently than you think. As a general rule of thumb, it's recommended to replace walking shoes every 300 to 500 miles (or every 3 to 5 months for those who walk for at least 45 minutes at least 3 times per week).

The specific lifespan of a shoe depends on several factors, including the frequency and intensity of use, the shoe's quality, and the type of surface you typically walk on. There are a few signs to look out for that may indicate it's time to replace your shoes:.

It has been revealed that ultimately, it's important to listen to your body and pay attention to any signs of discomfort or pain when walking. If you notice any of the above signs, it's a good idea to start looking for a fresh pair of walking shoes.

According to recent reports, "Starting slow and working your way up is better than overdoing it and giving up," Chris Gagliardi, a certified personal trainer at the American Council on Exercise, previously told Men's Health. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, according to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S.
  • Industry observers note that ‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor sees fresh ways to put Bitcoin (BTC) to work on Wall Street.

In a recent development, according to staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Bitcoin can be used to meet certain financial resource requirements for U.S. derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses.

Industry observers note that ‘Next step for adoption is using Bitcoin to work,’ Saylor wrote on X in response to the CFTC advisory published on Nov. 23.

As per the guidance, these companies must maintain sufficient financial resources to cover their operating costs for at least a year.

Industry observers note that as clarified by CFTC staff, Bitcoin and Ether can be used to meet this requirement (as well as payment stablecoins). The advisory also provides guidance on how staff interpret the current rules. It also applies to swap execution facilities (SEFs), which are platforms where counterparties trade swaps.

In a recent development, bitcoin holdings worth $10 million could count for $8 million toward the annual requirement, based on the minimum 20% discount that CFTC staff noted they would accept. This provides some flexibility in case Bitcoin's price falls. The discount is also called a haircut.

For Ether, the same minimum 20% haircut applies. For payment stablecoins, the haircut is 2%.

Sources indicate that this provides some incentive for an exchange to actually hold BTC. Exchanges could hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets and use some of its value to satisfy this reserve requirement. There would be no need to sell it for USD first.

Industry observers note that however, a futures exchange still needs to have sufficient unencumbered cash or highly liquid securities to cover its operating costs for at least six months. Bitcoin, Ether and even payment stablecoins do not fall into this category.

Recent findings suggest that the same six-month liquidity requirement applies to clearinghouses. Additionally, they need to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover a default by a clearing member.

CFTC staff also noted a potential downside for exchanges holding crypto reserves. During a market slump, there's a risk that an exchange's operating losses might rise. At the same time, the value of the Bitcoin it holds to cover those losses might fall.

So this possibility should be considered before an exchange decides whether to use Bitcoin to meet its financial resource requirements.

It has been revealed that onchain Lens reported over $600,000 lost from one user’s Trezor and Exodus wallets on the 23rd of November. The Trezor wallet theft report raised a harder question: how did transfers use the victim’s signing authority without their claimed approval?

The blockchain investigator listed approximately $580,000 in Tether [USDT] losses on TRON and $23,400 in USD Coin [USDC] on Solana. Another $9,500 reportedly disappeared from an Exodus wallet on the same iPhone 17 Pro Max.

Reportedly, the victim generated the recovery phrase on Trezor and kept it on paper and refused to allow anyone physical access to the device.

Recent findings suggest that A 49,999 USDT transfer on the 21st of November used the TRON account’s default owner permission. It was a direct transfer, with no transfer from operation drawing on an existing token allowance.

On Solana [SOL], the examined instruction identified the victim’s wallet as the transfer authority, signer, and fee payer. Notably, no separate delegate appeared.

It has been revealed that these transfers used the wallet’s signing authority. However, it is unclear how someone gained that access.

A valid signature authorizes a transaction on the network. So, it cannot establish whether the owner knowingly approved it. The Trezor accounts on both chains shared one recovery phrase, making that backup a possible link between the losses.

In an X reply, Trezor noted similar cases usually involved “a compromised wallet backup.”.

It’s hard to say what happened here without more details.

According to recent reports, the firm asked the affected user to contact official support. Its reply offered a possible explanation, without establishing this incident’s cause.

Trezor indicates its Bluetooth chip cannot access private keys. On the other hand, Exodus says its Trezor integration also leaves those keys inside the hardware. Whether the user enabled that integration remains unclear.

Apple’s 9th of November enhancement patched Bluetooth complications, but Onchain Lens found no evidence linking those vulnerabilities to these transfers.

Earlier incidents show why identifying the route matters.

As AMBCrypto reported, Trezor confirmed implants in three CryptoBilis-sold Safe 5 devices on the 12th of November. Those implants captured recovery words from device screens.

In a recent development, separately, Confiant’s MoldyRoost research documented another route; malicious ads delivering exploits to vulnerable iPhones. Furthermore, Chainalysis counted roughly 158,000 personal-wallet compromise incidents affecting 80,000 victims in 2025.

For this user, the unanswered question is specific: how did someone obtain signing access across the affected wallets?
